summary: Romania has been a full Schengen member since January 2025: EU citizens enter freely, visa-exempt nationalities such as the US and UK get 90 days in any 180-day period counted together with the rest of the Schengen Area, and other passports need a Schengen visa applied for via Romania's official eVisa portal. The currency remains the leu, not the euro.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

source.name: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 listing the third countries whose nationals must hold a visa — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Article 4(1) — stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024. Applications start on the official eVisa portal and are decided by the Romanian consulate serving your residence.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 16(1) (visa fee) and Article 1(1) (stays not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period), consolidated to 11 June 2024

fee.notes: €300 for long-stay visa applications submitted through the e-Viza portal from 27 April 2026 (€120 before that date). For stays over 90 days — work, study, family reunification and other long-stay purposes; converted into a residence permit after arrival.

source.name: e-Viza — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania: visa fees

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years. EU/EEA citizens only need a valid passport or national ID card.

source.name: e-Viza — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania: conditions of entry
e-Viza — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania: supporting documents

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 15(3) — travel medical insurance with minimum coverage of EUR 30 000

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

source.name: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), Article 6(1)(c) and Annex I (return or round-trip ticket as supporting evidence), consolidated to 12 October 2025

proofOfFunds.text: Romania's reference amount is €50 per person per day, and no less than €500 for the whole stay (€30 per day for those covered by the invitation procedure). Visa-exempt visitors are rarely asked but should be able to show means of support.

source.name: European Commission — Reference amounts required for the crossing of the external border, fixed by national authorities

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Between EU countries, alcohol and tobacco bought with tax paid, for your own use and not for resale, owe no further tax, according to the EU's Your Europe portal.

Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal gives a duty-free allowance of 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). Tobacco limits depend on the country, and travellers under 17 get no alcohol or tobacco allowance.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Romania's economy is primarily cash-based but that credit cards are widely accepted in major urban centres. It says exchanging money on the street is illegal, that euros can be exchanged at recognized exchange shops, banks and hotels, and that merchants may refuse well-worn banknotes.

safety.text: Romania is one of the EU's safer destinations with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing on public transport in Bucharest, unlicensed taxis (Canada's travel advice says not to hail one on the street), and stray dogs in some areas. Drones from the war in neighboring Ukraine have crossed into Romanian airspace and some carrying explosives have landed or washed ashore: follow RO-Alert warnings and do not approach military debris.

roadVignette.text: The rovinieta covers Romania's national roads, not only its motorways, and is registered to the number plate. Tariffs are set in lei and depend on the car's emission standard (Euro class), and the rovinieta is now sold through CNAIR's TollRo portal. The Fetești–Cernavodă bridge on the A2 toward the coast is tolled on top of the rovinieta — 19 RON per crossing for a car.

driving.text: Romania is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Romania yet.

tips.text: Romania's currency is the leu (RON), not the euro. Canada's travel advice says exchanging money on the street is illegal: change euros at recognized exchange shops, banks or hotels.

Since January 2025 Romania is a full Schengen member: no more checks at the land borders with Hungary and Bulgaria, and days spent in Romania count toward the same 90-in-180 allowance as France or Germany.

Before hiking or other activities in the Carpathians, Canada's travel advice says to check the Salvamont mountain rescue service for current risks. In an emergency, including wild animal encounters, the Romanian government sends RO-ALERT text messages to all active SIM cards.

Canada's travel advice says to use only licensed metered taxis that display their price lists, not to hail a taxi on the street but to order one from your hotel or use a trusted ride-sharing app, and at Bucharest's Henri Coandă airport to take a taxi from the booth in the arrivals terminal to get a fair rate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Romania?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens don't need a visa. Citizens of the Schengen visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan — can stay 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. Other nationalities need a Schengen short-stay visa, applied for through Romania's official eVisa portal (evisa.mae.ro) and the consulate serving their residence.

faq.question: Is Romania in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes. Romania joined Schengen for air and sea borders in March 2024 and became a full member — land borders included — on January 1, 2025. A Romanian-issued Schengen visa is valid for the whole area, and vice versa.

faq.question: Does Romania use the euro?
faq.answer: No. The currency is the Romanian leu (RON). Canada's travel advice says credit cards are widely accepted in major urban centres although the economy is primarily cash-based, and that euros should be exchanged at recognized exchange shops, banks or hotels; exchanging money on the street is illegal.

faq.question: Do days in Romania count toward the Schengen 90/180 limit?
faq.answer: Yes, since full Schengen membership in 2025 — time spent in Romania is counted together with days in all other Schengen countries. Before 2024 Romania had a separate 90-day allowance; that is no longer the case.

faq.question: Can Moldovan citizens travel to Romania visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes — Moldovan citizens with a biometric passport can enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU's visa-free regime; many Moldovans also hold Romanian (EU) citizenship, which gives full freedom of movement.
